request.prompt: Create exactly ONE faithful full-body 2D game sprite of Liara T'Soni wearing her Mass Effect 3 Alternate Appearance Pack 1 outfit. In BOTH supplied official BioWare screenshots, Liara is the blue-skinned asari on the FAR LEFT: reproduce only that character. Use the first image as authority for the full outfit, visible footwear and low-ready three-quarter stance facing toward the left of the image; the second image is a supplementary view of Liara's blue skin, head ridges and side details, not the framing. Preserve Liara's recognizable face and asari scalp crests without human hair. Precisely follow her black fitted suit, turquoise/cyan collar and chest bands, royal-blue chevron abdominal panel, small horizontal gold chest fasteners, silver shoulder caps, long black forearm guards with gold fittings, pale hip-mounted panels, thin gold seams and circular motifs on the thighs and shins, and tall black buckled boots. Retain the compact firearm held low in her two hands as visible in the first screenshot, with the same visible form, scale and light/dark material layout. Preserve the pose and anatomy rather than inventing a new costume or new combat action. Render as a detailed realistic game-asset cutout with neutral studio lighting and clear readable material distinctions, keeping blue skin blue despite the original screenshot's strong sunlight. Exactly one subject and one pose. Frame the entire head, hands, weapon, both legs and boot soles with comfortable transparent padding on all four sides; the whole figure should occupy about 80 percent of canvas height. Transparent background with no scene, floor, cast shadow, fire, smoke, glow, labels, logo, text, border, other character or additional view. Do not reproduce either the center or right-hand figures from the references.

notes: Liara is the far-left figure in both official BioWare screenshots.
First screenshot provides the full silhouette and boots; second is supplementary and darker.
Precise firearm model is not independently named; its visible shape is reference-bound.
Small motifs, occluded surfaces and palette under scene lighting remain unvalidated.
